samples.question: The cream page is littered with small decorative coloured squares that mean nothing; only the one dark slate SLAB decides the answer. The slab carries four square trays: one pale tray and three grey trays. Every tray holds a PILE of exactly three straight coloured bars, and all four piles use the same three bar colours. In each pile one bar - the SPINE - crosses the other two bars, and those two other bars never touch each other, so every pile shows exactly two places where two bars overlap. At each overlap one bar is laid ON TOP of the other and hides it there, so the colour you see in the overlap patch is the colour of the upper bar. Each pile has been turned or flipped on its tray independently of the others, so the direction a colour runs, where it sits and how thick the bars are carry no information: only which colour lies on top at each overlap matters. The pile on the pale tray is the KEY. Exactly one of the three grey trays holds a pile in which BOTH over/under facts are the same as the key's - the same colour on top of the same colour at both overlaps - and the other two grey piles reverse at least one of them. Each grey tray is labelled by one small marker square in its top-left corner, coloured orange, teal, magenta or olive; marker colours are assigned at random and are never bar colours. What is the marker colour of the grey tray whose pile repeats both of the key pile's over/under facts? Answer orange, teal, magenta or olive.
